answer: A deposit-backed reputation ridge works like this: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can vouch for others, and the stake sits on a public ridge anyone can inspect. New identities start with no trust and earn it slowly through verified work, so each fake agent must be funded separately. An attacker faces a spiral of rising costs: every sybil needs its own stake, history and fees, while one detected fraud burns the whole stake. Like a jetty breaking a wave into smaller pieces, the stake fragments an attacker budget so a flood of fake identities becomes too expensive to sustain.
